Hi Judy — thanks for the clear list. Summary below and I attached a short annex and our SOC 2 report for completeness.

Residency:
- Hosted (Redwood API): For customers who require US-only residency we can pin tenant storage and request routing to us-east-1. This prevents active request routing and primary logs from being stored outside that region.
- We offer a formal residency addendum for contractual binding; see attached "redwood-data-residency-annex_v2.pdf".

Retention & deletion:
- Default logs/telemetry: 30 days for request traces and aggregated metrics.
- Request payloads (customer-provided content): by default retained for 30 days to support troubleshooting and billing.
- Shorter windows: We support custom retention windows down to 0 days (delete on ingest) for hosted tenants under an enterprise addendum. Process: sign residency/addendum -> configuration flag set -> we perform a one-time backfill deletion for the shorter window.

Training usage assurance:
- Short answer: Redwood does not use production customer content from hosted or dedicated customers to train or improve our public or internal models, unless the customer explicitly opts in (rare, opt-in only, and always documented in the contract).
- For clarity: telemetry and aggregated usage signals (token volumes, non-content performance metrics) may be used for capacity planning and anonymized product telemetry; these are not used to train model weights.
- Private/On-prem: customers running Redwood Private control the compute and storage; we do not have access and thus cannot use that data for training.

Next steps: I can provide a one-page statement tailored for your security questionnaire and loop in Legal for contractual language. Camila will follow up on procurement and the proposed MAP (Mutual Action Plan).

Regards,

Hi Judy — quick operational notes on the retention workflow: 

- If Acme signs the residency addendum we set an account-level cfg (region_pin: us-east-1) and a retention_ttl (default 30 -> requested value).
- Backfill deletion: Once the shorter TTL is effective we run a controlled backfill to delete any existing data older than the new TTL. We provide an export of deleted object ids for audit if requested.
- Deletion verification: We can provide an automated deletion report and a signed attestation (one-off) for enterprise customers.

I'm attaching a proposed Mutual Action Plan with milestones (see proposed-MAP-acmehealth.xlsx). If you want, Priya can own the legal coordination for the addendum text.

Hi Judy — attaching proposed contract text and a short questionnaire answer you can paste into Acme's security form.

Proposed clause (draft):
'Customer Content' means any data, text, or files submitted by Customer to Redwood Inference for processing. Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any of Redwood's models or third-party models unless Redwood has obtained Customer's explicit, written authorization for such use. This restriction applies to model training, evaluation sets, and public release. 

Support and debug data: Redwood may collect ephemeral debug traces when required to investigate incidents or support requests. Ephemeral traces are retained only as necessary for the investigation and are deleted within the configured retention window unless the customer has requested otherwise. All support access is logged and subject to audit.

Machine-readable deletion manifest:
- We can produce a CSV manifest with object ids, deletion timestamp (RFC3339), and an HMAC signature over the file for attestation. This will be included in the enterprise addendum as an optional deliverable.

I'll loop in Legal for final wording but happy to start here.

Regards,
